dataset_family: Far Eastern Memorial Hospital / National Yang-Ming University MMSE facial-video sample (Taiwan): 45 participants (32 CN / 13 MCI), 48 videos; private
method_family: Facial-video deep learning: multi-stream CNN (RGB frame + x/y optical-flow streams, ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18/34/50 backbones), segment classification with participant-level majority vote
what_it_shows: Facial videos recorded while participants took the (interviewer-administered) MMSE are classified MCI vs CN by a multi-stream CNN. On a 9-participant validation set that also served as the test set, the best segment-level accuracy is 0.87 (ResNet-18) and 0.90 (ResNet-50). Participant-level accuracy is 1.00 (ResNet-18, 9/9) and 0.89 (ResNet-50); ResNet-34 gives 0.61 (segment) and 0.56 (participant). The capture device is not described. The MCI diagnostic criteria are not described. No external validation, no head-to-head.
why: Lee et al., BMC Bioinformatics (ICBEI supplement; received 2022, accepted 2024; DOI 10.1186/s12859-024-05911-6). It is a full peer-reviewed article with results, not a conference abstract and not a preprint. The PDF title, authors and DOI match the block and the map entry. Against Table A1 it supports only 'high standalone accuracy'. The videos were recorded 'while participating in the MMSE' (p.4), i.e. an interviewer-administered session, so the instrument is not self-administered. 'Consumer-grade' cannot be confirmed: no camera is named, only mixed resolutions (1920x1080, 1280x720, 640x480; p.4). This is the same status round 20 gave P-76/P-77 (partly). Against the narrowed wording it fits on every component. (1) Low-cost behavioural data without specialist hardware: plain facial video with no specialist sensor, and the authors call the approach 'inexpensive' (p.1, p.14). The device-grade point rests on the modality and the authors' claim, not on a described device. (2) Best-case standalone accuracy of about 88-94%: segment 0.87-0.90, participant 0.89 (ResNet-50), and 1.00 (ResNet-18) above the band. (3) Small internally validated sample, with a weaker configuration at 0.56-0.61 matching the wording's 'other themes and repeated splits' range. (4) No external validation, no head-to-head. The evidence is very thin, and the record must say so. There is no separate test set: 'The verification set will be used in the model testing phase' (p.8-9). The best checkpoint per training run is 'stored and used for testing' (p.10), and 27 configurations are compared on that same 9-participant set. So the participant-level figures rest on 3 MCI and 6 CN people and are selected on the test data itself. This is the same defect round 20 recorded for P-76, but with a smaller evaluation set. Also, '13 are diagnosed with MCI' is stated without diagnostic criteria (p.4). Independence: a Taiwanese hospital sample (Yuan Ze University; NYCU; Far Eastern Memorial Hospital). No overlap with I-CONECT or the Denver/Harvard authors of P-76/P-77, nor with P-101's Shanghai/Henan sample, nor with the other candidates. Method family: facial-video deep learning, the same broad modality family as P-76 (ViViT) and P-77 (STAM) but a different architecture (two-stream CNN on optical flow), on an independent dataset. If admitted, it would broaden the facial-video strand beyond I-CONECT. It would not add a self-administered instrument.

quotes.quote: There are 45 participants in this study, 32 are cognitively normal (median age 69 years, IQR 67–73 years, 9 males, 23 females) and 13 are diagnosed with MCI (median age 75 years, IQR 71–78 years, 6 males, 7 females).
In order to collect realistic and reasonable data from participants without stress or embarrassment, participants recorded videos while participating in the MMSE.
Several types of resolutions are used in the original videos, such as 1920 × 1080, 1280 × 720, and 640 × 480.

There are 4237 segments (36 participants, 39 videos) in the training set and 917 segments (9 participants, 9 videos) in the validation set.
